ios-page-structures|Windows.summary: A Plenix window on iPadOS is the system window (a WindowGroup scene), with the system frame, window controls, resizing and multitasking left exactly as the system draws them. Plenix styles only what the app owns inside the window, the way the Web AppShell does: the Plenix canvas behind the content, a sidebar in the Plenix pane surface with a 44-point header area, DM Sans titles at the heading role, and a layout that adapts smoothly to every size the window can take. The system window frame is never imitated.

variants.name: Window with sidebar
variants.use: The main window of an app with several areas: the sidebar and the content side by side.

variants.name: Inactive window
variants.use: A window that is open but not in front; the system draws its frame and controls inactive.

anatomy.name: Window frame
anatomy.about: The system frame, corners and shadow; Plenix never draws or restyles it.

anatomy.name: Window controls
anatomy.about: The system close, minimize and full-screen controls at the leading top corner.

anatomy.name: Sidebar
anatomy.about: The optional leading pane in the Plenix pane surface, with the Plenix sidebar rows.

anatomy.name: Header area
anatomy.about: The 44-point area at the top of each pane for the title and toolbar items, clear of the window controls.

anatomy.name: Content
anatomy.about: The main pane on the Plenix canvas; it adapts to every window size.
